## Description {#details}

<p>Functions for comparing actual and expected values in tests.</p>


<p>A check written as a plain boolean, such as <span class="doxyComputerOutput">t.expect (x == 42)</span>, reports only its location when it fails. The function comparators compare two values and, when the check fails, also report both values:</p>


<table class="doxyTable">
<tr>
<th>Comparator</th>
<th>True when</th>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::eq (a, b)</span></td>
<td><span class="doxyComputerOutput">a == b</span></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::ne (a, b)</span></td>
<td><span class="doxyComputerOutput">a != b</span></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::lt (a, b)</span></td>
<td><span class="doxyComputerOutput">a &lt; b</span></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::le (a, b)</span></td>
<td><span class="doxyComputerOutput">a &lt;= b</span></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::gt (a, b)</span></td>
<td><span class="doxyComputerOutput">a &gt; b</span></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::ge (a, b)</span></td>
<td><span class="doxyComputerOutput">a &gt;= b</span></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::approx (a, b, e)</span></td>
<td><span class="doxyComputerOutput">a</span> and <span class="doxyComputerOutput">b</span> differ by at most <span class="doxyComputerOutput">e</span></td>
</tr>
</table>

<dl class="doxySectionUser">
<dt>Example</dt>
<dd></dd>
</dl>


<div class="doxyProgramListing">

<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">ts.test (</span><span class="doxyHighlightStringLiteral">"Check various conditions"</span><span class="doxyHighlight">, [] (</span><span class="doxyHighlightKeyword">auto</span><span class="doxyHighlight">&amp; t) {</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">  t.expect (mt::eq (compute_answer (), 42)) &lt;&lt; </span><span class="doxyHighlightStringLiteral">"answer is 42"</span><span class="doxyHighlight">;</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">  t.expect (mt::ne (compute_answer (), 43)) &lt;&lt; </span><span class="doxyHighlightStringLiteral">"answer is not 43"</span><span class="doxyHighlight">;</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">  t.expect (mt::lt (compute_answer (), 43)) &lt;&lt; </span><span class="doxyHighlightStringLiteral">"answer is &lt; 43"</span><span class="doxyHighlight">;</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">  t.expect (mt::le (compute_answer (), 43)) &lt;&lt; </span><span class="doxyHighlightStringLiteral">"answer is &lt;= 43"</span><span class="doxyHighlight">;</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">  t.expect (mt::gt (compute_answer (), 41)) &lt;&lt; </span><span class="doxyHighlightStringLiteral">"answer is &gt; 41"</span><span class="doxyHighlight">;</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">  t.expect (mt::ge (compute_answer (), 42)) &lt;&lt; </span><span class="doxyHighlightStringLiteral">"answer is &gt;= 42"</span><span class="doxyHighlight">;</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">});</span></span></div>

</div>


<p>When <span class="doxyComputerOutput">compute_answer()</span> returns 41, the human-readable reporter displays the failed checks with the compared values:</p>


<div class="doxyProgramListing">

<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">• Check various conditions</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">    ✗ answer is 42 FAILED (main.cpp:21, 41 == 42)</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">    ✗ answer is &gt; 41 FAILED (main.cpp:25, 41 &gt; 41)</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">    ✗ answer is &gt;= 42 FAILED (main.cpp:26, 41 &gt;= 42)</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">✗ Check various conditions - FAILED (3 checks passed, 3 failed)</span></span></div>

</div>


<dl class="doxySectionUser">
<dt>How the values are compared</dt>
<dd>
<ul class="doxyList ">
<li>The operands must be comparable with the operator of the comparator; for example, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::eq (a, b)</span> does not compile when <span class="doxyComputerOutput">a == b</span> would not.</li>
<li>Integers of different signedness are compared by value, as by <span class="doxyComputerOutput">std::cmp_equal()</span>: <span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::eq (-1, static_cast&lt;unsigned&gt; (-1))</span> fails, although <span class="doxyComputerOutput">-1 == static_cast&lt;unsigned&gt; (-1)</span> is true. The single characters (<span class="doxyComputerOutput">char</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">wchar_t</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">char8_t</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">char16_t</span>, and <span class="doxyComputerOutput">char32_t</span>) are compared in the same way, as the integers of the same size and signedness.</li>
<li>C strings (the arrays, including the string literals, and the pointers of <span class="doxyComputerOutput">char</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">wchar_t</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">char8_t</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">char16_t</span>, and <span class="doxyComputerOutput">char32_t</span>) are compared by content, also with the standard strings and string views of the same character type, so <span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::eq (actual, "abc")</span> checks the characters, not the addresses. The text of an array ends at its first null character, or at its end. A null pointer is equal only to another null pointer (or <span class="doxyComputerOutput">nullptr</span>), not to an empty string.</li>
<li>Other arrays (including <span class="doxyComputerOutput">uint8_t</span> buffers) are compared element by element, also with a container, with the elements compared as the single values are.</li>
<li>Other pointers are compared by address.</li>
<li>The application types need an <span class="doxyComputerOutput">operator&lt;&lt;</span> for the formatter, which writes their values in the report; without it, the comparator does not compile. See <a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/groups/micro-os-plus-micro-test-plus-cpp-api-customisation">Customisation</a>.</li>
</ul>
</dd>
</dl>


<dl class="doxySectionUser">
<dt>Cost and lifetime of the operands</dt>
<dd><p>A comparator moves the temporaries into the expression that it returns, and copies the named operands, for every check, passing or failing, so a large container or string costs an allocation; compare a <span class="doxyComputerOutput">std::string_view</span> of the string instead, when the cost matters. Since the expression holds its own copies, it can be returned from the function that builds it, and kept after the operands are destroyed. The exceptions are the arrays and the characters of the C strings, which are only referred to and must outlive the expression.</p></dd>
</dl>


<dl class="doxySectionUser">
<dt>Comparing approximately</dt>
<dd>
<p>The comparison of floating-point values with <span class="doxyComputerOutput">eq()</span> is exact, so <span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::eq (0.1 + 0.2, 0.3)</span> fails. To accept a difference, use <span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::approx (a, b, epsilon)</span>, which is true when the operands differ by at most <span class="doxyComputerOutput">epsilon</span>, the limit included:</p>


<ul class="doxyList ">
<li>the operands and the tolerance are integral or floating-point numbers, of any such type, except <span class="doxyComputerOutput">bool</span> and the character types (<span class="doxyComputerOutput">char</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">wchar_t</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">char8_t</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">char16_t</span>, and <span class="doxyComputerOutput">char32_t</span>), which are not numbers and are rejected; <span class="doxyComputerOutput">signed char</span> and <span class="doxyComputerOutput">unsigned char</span> are accepted. The distance of integers is computed exactly, also for operands of different signedness;</li>
<li>a negative tolerance fails all the comparisons;</li>
<li>a failed check shows the operands and the tolerance, as in <span class="doxyComputerOutput">1.0 ~ (1.5 +/- 0.1)</span>.</li>
</ul>
</dd>
</dl>


<div class="doxyProgramListing">

<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">ts.test (</span><span class="doxyHighlightStringLiteral">"Check approximate values"</span><span class="doxyHighlight">, [] (</span><span class="doxyHighlightKeyword">auto</span><span class="doxyHighlight">&amp; t) {</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">  t.expect (mt::approx (read_adc (), 512, 3)) &lt;&lt; </span><span class="doxyHighlightStringLiteral">"ADC reading"</span><span class="doxyHighlight">;</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">  t.expect (mt::approx (compute_float (), 42.0f, 0.001f))</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">      &lt;&lt; </span><span class="doxyHighlightStringLiteral">"result is about 42"</span><span class="doxyHighlight">;</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">});</span></span></div>

</div>


<dl class="doxySectionUser">
<dt>Comparing containers</dt>
<dd><p>Containers are compared with their own operators, so they must be comparable, usually by being of the same type. When the check fails, the elements of both containers are shown, up to the first 16; when two longer containers differ after them, the report adds the index of the first difference.</p></dd>
</dl>


<div class="doxyProgramListing">

<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">ts.test (</span><span class="doxyHighlightStringLiteral">"Check containers"</span><span class="doxyHighlight">, [] (</span><span class="doxyHighlightKeyword">auto</span><span class="doxyHighlight">&amp; t) {</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">  t.expect (mt::eq (std::vector&lt;int&gt;{ 1, 2 }, std::vector&lt;int&gt;{ 1, 2 }))</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">      &lt;&lt; </span><span class="doxyHighlightStringLiteral">"vector{ 1, 2 } eq vector{ 1, 2 }"</span><span class="doxyHighlight">;</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">  t.expect (mt::ne (std::vector&lt;int&gt;{ 1, 2, 3 },</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">                    std::vector&lt;int&gt;{ 1, 2, 4 }))</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">      &lt;&lt; </span><span class="doxyHighlightStringLiteral">"vector{ 1, 2, 3 } ne vector{ 1, 2, 4 }"</span><span class="doxyHighlight">;</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">});</span></span></div>

</div>

## Functions

### approx() {#ga0d374ffc56933dccd3ffba008ab7eaa5}

<div class="doxyMemberItem">
<div class="doxyMemberProto">
<div class="doxyMemberTemplate">template &lt;class Lhs_T, class Rhs_T, class Epsilon_T&gt;</div>
<table class="doxyMemberLabels">
<tr class="doxyMemberLabels">
<td class="doxyMemberLabelsLeft">
<table class="doxyMemberName">
<tr>
<td class="doxyMemberName">auto micro_os_plus::micro_test_plus::approx (Lhs_T &amp;&amp; lhs, Rhs_T &amp;&amp; rhs, Epsilon_T &amp;&amp; epsilon)</td>
</tr>
</table>
</td>
<td class="doxyMemberLabelsRight">
<span class="doxyMemberLabels">
<span class="doxyMemberLabel nodiscard">nodiscard</span>
<span class="doxyMemberLabel constexpr">constexpr</span>
</span>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Approximate equality comparator, with an explicit tolerance.</p>


<p>The comparison succeeds if the distance between <span class="doxyComputerOutput">lhs</span> and <span class="doxyComputerOutput">rhs</span> is less than or equal to <span class="doxyComputerOutput">epsilon</span>, so a tolerance of zero requires equal values. The operands are numbers, integral or floating-point, possibly of different types (the deprecated value wrappers and numeric literals are also accepted, and their own tolerance is not used). For the integers, the distance is computed exactly, also for operands of different signedness, so <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/groups/micro-os-plus-micro-test-plus-cpp-api-deprecated-literals/#gafe47800a219b00fcccf0a1dc596dbe20">approx</a> (0u, -1, 2)</span> succeeds; for the other types, in their common floating-point type. A failure is reported as <span class="doxyComputerOutput">lhs ~ (rhs +/- epsilon)</span>.</p>


<div class="doxyProgramListing">

<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">t.expect (mt::approx (read_adc (), 512, 3)) &lt;&lt; </span><span class="doxyHighlightStringLiteral">"ADC reading"</span><span class="doxyHighlight">;</span></span></div>
<div class="doxyCodeLine"><span class="doxyNoLineNumber">&nbsp;</span><span class="doxyLineContent"><span class="doxyHighlight">t.expect (mt::approx (compute_float (), 42.0f, 0.001f));</span></span></div>

</div>


<p>The deprecated <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/groups/micro-os-plus-micro-test-plus-cpp-api-deprecated-literals/#gafe47800a219b00fcccf0a1dc596dbe20">approx</a> (value, epsilon)</span> form, available only with <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/groups/micro-os-plus-micro-test-plus-config/#ga67c701de5426ac340584ed038494a873">MICRO_OS_PLUS_MICRO_TEST_PLUS_DEPRECATED_ENABLED</a></span>, is a value wrapper instead, which applies its tolerance to the six comparisons and to the operators; it accepts only floating-point values.</p>

### eq() {#ga0fbc0f7ddf0107c1e5265bb79287487d}

<div class="doxyMemberItem">
<div class="doxyMemberProto">
<div class="doxyMemberTemplate">template &lt;class Lhs_T, class Rhs_T&gt;</div>

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Generic equality comparator.</p>


<p>The C strings (the arrays, including the string literals, and the pointers of <span class="doxyComputerOutput">char</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">wchar_t</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">char8_t</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">char16_t</span>, and <span class="doxyComputerOutput">char32_t</span>) are compared by content, also with the standard strings and string views of the same character type; a null pointer is equal only to another null pointer, and the text of an array ends at its first null character, or at its end. The other arrays (e.g. byte buffers) are compared element by element, also with a container, with the elements compared as the single values are, and written as ranges; the other pointers are compared by address. The integers of different signedness are compared by value, as by <span class="doxyComputerOutput">std::cmp_equal()</span>, not after the usual arithmetic conversions, so <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="#ga0fbc0f7ddf0107c1e5265bb79287487d">eq</a> (-1, static_cast&lt;unsigned&gt; (-1))</span> fails; the single characters take part as the integers of the same size and signedness.</p>


<p>Both operands must satisfy <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/concepts/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/extension/printable">extension::printable</a></span>, since they are reported on failure; an application type needs an <span class="doxyComputerOutput">operator&lt;&lt;</span> for <span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::expression_formatter</span>, otherwise the call is rejected, with a diagnostic that names the operand type. The operands must also be comparable with the operator of the comparator, otherwise the call is rejected in the same way.</p>


<p>The same rules apply to <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="#ga92cdc2dde6af040f2f5f5df677df0985">ne()</a></span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="#ga90da2cbc14b4562332a205d5b232356f">gt()</a></span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="#ga58c7dacabca3fe1b0dc025a0e0f30e9e">ge()</a></span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="#ga493a42c738ef38b45a28b06a2155aa00">lt()</a></span>, and <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="#ga9125d2dd997269eecc0d8239d5df67e5">le()</a></span>.</p>

<dl class="doxySectionUser">
<dt>Returns</dt>
<dd><p>A comparator object that evaluates to true if the operands are equal.</p></dd>
</dl>


<p>The <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="#ga0fbc0f7ddf0107c1e5265bb79287487d">eq</a></span> function template provides a generic equality comparator for any types. The operands are first passed to <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/namespaces/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/#a51e86043001b197561806d5c6297041b">detail::as_operand()</a></span>, which converts the C strings to <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/structs/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/basic-c-string">detail::basic_c_string</a></span>, and the other arrays to <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/structs/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/array-operand">detail::array_operand</a></span>, so that they are compared by content. It constructs a comparator object, with the <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/structs/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/equal-to">detail::equal_to</a></span> tag, which evaluates to <span class="doxyComputerOutput">true</span> if the two values are equal, and which is reported with both values if not.</p>


<p>The operands are forwarded, so that the comparator moves the temporaries, and copies the named operands (see <span class="doxyComputerOutput">stored_operand_t</span>), so that the expression stays valid after the operands are destroyed, except for the arrays and the C strings, which are referred to.</p>
